name: Cross device identity linking
plain: A site recognises one person across phone, laptop and tablet when they sign in on each.
meaning: A shared login ID is a deterministic link. Hashed email, phone and shared IP add probabilistic links. Ad platforms with big login bases (Google, Meta, Apple) see the same person across devices; others rent graphs like UID2 or RampID.

web.api: Account ID in first party cookie or token; hashed email in ad requests

access.persistence: Linked for as long as the account and ID graph entry exist
access.revocation: Clear site data, browser privacy settings

limits.headline: Can recognize you as one person across your phone, laptop and tablet when you sign in
limits.user_action: You sign in on each device with the same account or email.
can: Link your devices through the same account
Match you using a scrambled copy of your email in ad requests
Carry your history and recommendations from one device to the next
cannot: Link a device you never signed in on, except by guesswork
Match you if you use a different account or email on each device

story.what_it_is: A site recognises you as one person across your phone, laptop and tablet when you sign in on each.
story.for_you: You do not see it. Because you sign in on each device, the site can show your history on all of them, and also connect your habits across them.
story.for_makers: Makers use it for better service, like continuing a video where you left off. Advertisers use it to follow a person across devices and measure which ad on one device led to a purchase on another.

use_cases.example: You pause a show on your laptop and it resumes on your phone at the same minute.
You add an item on your phone and see it in your cart on your laptop.
An advertiser sees that you saw an ad on your phone and bought on your laptop, and counts it as a win.
A browser game keeps your progress on every device that you sign in on.
A bank spots a login from a new device and asks for another step.
A social site shows the same feed and drafts on every device.
A team counts one person as one user across devices to get the true audience size.

technical_bounds: Needs the person to sign in on each device
Hash matching needs the vendor's own copy of the email
Safari and Firefox limit cross-site ID passing

legit_uses: Same account on any device, cross device frequency caps
abuse: Profile joining across devices without clear consent

history.change: FTC says hashing does not anonymise personal identifiers

refs.label: FTC: hashing doesn't make data anonymous
